decisionsTitle: The calendar's address, to copy, and what to do when Google says it already has it (amending §107)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-08, twice:** «Why can't I add the event back to my Google calendar after I removed it?» and «Still can't re-import the Brașov Runners calendar».

**What happened.** Nothing on the site. The feed and the event files answered as always; Google Calendar did three things that look like a broken button.

1. *The Bin.* A deleted event sits in the calendar's Bin for 30 days, and a file carrying the same event — the same `UID`, on purpose (§107, §174), so an edit updates the entry instead of adding a second — is ignored meanwhile.
2. *Hide is not unsubscribe.* The «×» beside a calendar in Google's left list hides it. The calendar is still there, unticked under the settings.
3. *The per-address cache.* Google keeps a URL calendar it has seen by its address. The site's «Google Calendar» button is Google's quick-add link (`https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r?cid=webcal://…`, `calendarFeedLinks`); for an address Google believes it already has, the press does nothing, or adds a calendar that stays empty for up to a day.

What always works: calendar.google.com on the web → «+» beside «Alte calendare» → «Din URL» → the feed's address, with `?v=2` at the end when Google says it already has it. The Google Calendar phone app cannot add a calendar by address at all; the phone's browser can.

**Decision.** The address joins the button; the button stays, because it works the first time and is one press.

- *The calendar page.* The «?» fold beside the heading on a phone (§487) and the fold under «Adaugă în calendarul tău» (renamed «Adresa calendarului, de copiat», amending §195) each hold a read-only box with the feed's plain `https://…/<locale>/events/calendar.ics` address, from `APP_BASE_URL`, and «Copiază» beside it. Under them, three lines, each under 200 characters: «Nu merge butonul? Google ascunde calendarul în loc să-l scoată și ține o copie veche după adresă.», «Pe web: calendar.google.com → „+” lângă „Alte calendare” → „Din URL” → lipește adresa, cu ?v=2 la final.», «Aplicația Google Calendar de pe telefon nu adaugă un calendar după adresă; folosește site-ul.» §195 had made the folded address a `webcal://` link, to press as well as to copy; the «Apple / Outlook / telefon» button beside it is that same link, so the fold now holds the address to paste, in `https://`, which «Din URL» and every other app take.
- *The event page.* Under «Adaugă în calendar:», a closed fold «Adresa fișierului, de copiat» with the event's own file (`…/<locale>/events/<slug>/calendar.ics`) in the same box and «Ai șters evenimentul din Google Calendar? Îl găsești 30 de zile în Coșul calendarului, pe web; fișierul acesta nu se adaugă a doua oară cât timp e acolo.» A members' event (§552) has no fold: its file opens with a member's session only, which Google does not have.
- *One clipboard island.* «Copiază» is `CopyCodeButton` (§552, already the members' codes and «Ce le spui»), handed strings only; the page stays a Server Component. It now says «Copiat» for two seconds (it was two and a half), and where the browser refuses the clipboard (plain HTTP, an old browser, a webview) it selects the box's text so a long-press or Ctrl+C takes it (`copy-text.ts`); before, a refusal did nothing. The box is a read-only `<input>` at 16 pixels on a phone, so iOS does not zoom when it takes the focus; the button is 44 pixels.
- *The words in English* say the same, with Google's English labels («From URL», «Other calendars», «Bin»).

**`?v=2` is harmless.** Both `.ics` routes are `force-static` route handlers (§549) that read nothing of the request. Next 16.3 hands a `force-static` handler a request whose search params are emptied (`forceStaticRequestHandlers`), and keys the kept copy by the path alone (`cacheKey = resolvedPathname` in `app-route`'s template), so `?v=2` is served from the same cache entry as the bare address, not fetched fresh (read in Next's code, not measured on a server). On Vercel the CDN's copy is expected to be the same one, a prerender's allowed query being the route's own parameters (not measured; to read after the QA deploy: `curl -sI …/calendar.ics?v=2` says `x-vercel-cache: HIT` once the bare address has been asked). The proxy never sees either file: its matcher skips every path with a dot. Either way the body is the same bytes, and a stranger's `?v=`, `?slug=` or `?from=` changes nothing — an integration test asks both routes with and without queries and compares the bodies. The feed and the files are byte for byte unchanged.

**The FAQ.** The platform ships no FAQ entry about the calendar (the FAQ is the club's own text, written in «Pagini» → «Întrebări frecvente»), so there is no template to change; the same two facts are in `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` § Google Calendar will not add the calendar again, for whoever is asked next.

**Refused.**
- *A new `UID` per download*, so a deleted event could be imported again at once: every later edit would add a second entry instead of updating the first, the very thing §107 and §174 chose the event's `UID` to prevent.
- *A `?v=` the site rotates itself* in the button's address: to Google every new value is a new calendar, so each visit to the page would offer a second, third, fourth «🏃 BVR».
- *Dropping the quick-add button* for the address alone: it works the first time for nearly everybody, in one press, and the address is now under it for the rest.
- *A second clipboard component* for the calendar: the members' one is extended instead.

**Amends §107** (the calendar's doors gain the address to copy), **§195** (the folded address is a box to copy, no longer a `webcal://` link).
changelogLine: - **The calendar's address, to copy** — the calendar page and each event page show the feed's (or the event file's) plain address with «Copiază», and say what to do when Google Calendar's button does nothing: calendar.google.com → «Din URL», with `?v=2` at the end; a deleted event waits 30 days in Google's Bin. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the calendar page, when it renders, then the «?» fold beside the heading and the fold «Adresa calendarului, de copiat» under «Adaugă în calendarul tău» each hold a read-only box with the feed's plain `https://…/<locale>/events/calendar.ics` address from `APP_BASE_URL` and «Copiază», which puts the address on the clipboard and says «Copiat» for two seconds, or selects the box's text where the clipboard is refused; under the box, three lines under 200 characters in each language: Google hides a calendar rather than removing it and keeps a copy by its address; calendar.google.com → «+» → «Din URL» with `?v=2` at the end; the phone app cannot add a calendar by address. Google Calendar's quick-add button and the `webcal://` button stay (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a published public event with a date, when its page renders, then under «Adaugă în calendar:» a closed fold «Adresa fișierului, de copiat» holds the event's own `…/<locale>/events/<slug>/calendar.ics` address in the same box with «Copiază», and the sentence that a deleted event waits 30 days in Google Calendar's Bin, during which the file is not added again; a members' event has no such fold (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given `/<locale>/events/calendar.ics` or `/<locale>/events/<slug>/calendar.ics` asked with a query — `?v=2`, `?v=3`, or any key a stranger adds — then the answer's status, type, disposition and body are the bare address's, byte for byte: neither handler reads the request (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
At 320 px the calendar page's «?» fold shows the feed's address box and a «Copiază» button at least 44 pixels tall, with no horizontal scroll (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the calendar's address to copy, and Google's «Din URL» with ?v=2
